question: How many recipients of the Arjuna Award were there in the inaugural edition of Arjuna Award in 1961?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**20**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Arjuna Award** was instituted in **1961** by the Government of India to recognize outstanding achievement in sports.
 
• In its inaugural edition, a total of **20 recipients** were honored with the prestigious award.
 
• The award is named after **Arjuna**, one of the central characters in the Indian epic **Mahabharata**, symbolizing skills and courage in sports.
 
• The recipients in the first year represented diverse sports disciplines, showcasing the breadth of talent across the country.
 
• The award initially focused on recognizing **individual excellence** in sports but has evolved over time to include contributions to team events and coaching.
 
• Recipients of the Arjuna Award are honored with a **bronze statuette of Arjuna**, a **certificate**, and a **cash prize**.
 
• The Arjuna Award is considered one of the most prestigious recognitions for sportspersons in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Arjuna Award Evolution**__

 __
 
• Over the years, the criteria for the Arjuna Award have been refined to include achievements at the **national level**, **international events**, and contributions toward the promotion of sports.
 
• The award now also recognizes contributions made by coaches under the **Dronacharya Award category**.
 
• It is awarded annually by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, Government of India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Sports Awards in India**__
 
 
• India celebrates sporting excellence through awards like the **Arjuna Award**, **Dronacharya Award**, **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna** (now known as Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna), and others.
 
• These awards aim to inspire young athletes and promote a culture of sportsmanship across the nation.
 
• They also help in fostering a sense of pride and recognition for sportspersons who excel against global competition.
